subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the lines represented by (lx + my)² − 3(mx − ly)² = 0 together with the line lx + my + n = 0 form an equilateral triangle whose area is n² / (√3(l² + m²)) square units.

mark_split.label: Split the pair into two lines
Find the angle between L and L₁

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 4 PAIR OF STRAIGHT LINES, Short Answer question 15(i), book p.170. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split is 1+1+1+1 because the question asks for two things — that the triangle is equilateral, and its area — and each half needs two steps: the pair must be split before an angle can be measured, and the angles must be settled before the height can be turned into a side. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say how you get the two lines out of the pair, and what you measure to show the triangle is equilateral.

steps.label: Split the pair into two lines
steps.margin_note: First mark. The pair is already a difference of two squares, so no middle term has to be split — take √3 inside the second bracket and use A² − B² = (A − B)(A + B).
steps.memory_tip: It is already A² − B², so use (A − B)(A + B) — no middle term to split.
lines: Given line L: lx + my + n = 0   ……(2)
(1) is a difference of two squares:

recall.must_convey: That the pair is a difference of two squares and splits into L₁ and L₂ with √3 inside.
accept: it is A squared minus B squared so it factorises as A minus B into A plus B
take root three inside the second bracket
the two lines are l minus root three m into x plus m plus root three l into y equals zero and the other with the signs swapped
difference of squares ga factorise cheyyali
collect the x terms and the y terms in each factor

steps.why: Both lines of the pair pass through the origin, so the origin is one vertex of the triangle and the given line cuts off the other two.
common_mistakes: Leaving the 3 outside as a factor instead of writing it as (√3)².
Collecting only the x terms and leaving the y terms uncombined.

steps.label: Find the angle between L and L₁
steps.margin_note: One mark. Measure the angle through the normals: the angle between two lines equals the angle between their normal vectors. Both cross terms in the dot product cancel, which is the whole point of the √3.
steps.memory_tip: Measure through the NORMALS — the √3 terms in the dot product cancel each other.
lines: Dot product = l² − √3lm + m² + √3lm = l² + m²
So the length of L₁'s normal is 2√(l² + m²)

recall.must_convey: That the dot product of the two normals is l² + m² and the lengths give cos θ₁ = ½, so θ₁ = 60°.
accept: the angle between two lines is the angle between their normals
the dot product comes out l squared plus m squared because the root three terms cancel
the second normal has length two root l squared plus m squared
normals madhya angle teesukovali, root three terms cancel avuthaayi
cos theta is one half so the angle is sixty degrees

steps.why: Using normals avoids slopes altogether, so the proof never has to treat a vertical line as a separate case.
common_mistakes: Taking (l, m) as a direction vector of L instead of its normal.
Expanding (l − √3m)² as l² − √3lm + 3m² and losing the factor 2.

steps.label: Show all three angles are 60°
steps.margin_note: One mark. The second line gives the same working with the sign of √3 reversed, so the same cancellation happens. Two angles of 60° force the third to be 60° as well.
steps.memory_tip: Two angles of 60° force the third one, because the three angles add to 180°.
lines: For L and L₂ the normals are (l, m)
Dot product = l² + √3lm + m² − √3lm = l² + m²
All three angles are 60°, so the triangle

recall.must_convey: That L₂ gives cos θ₂ = ½ by the same working, so all three angles are 60° and the triangle is equilateral.
accept: the second line gives the same result with the sign of root three reversed
both angles at the given line are sixty degrees
the third angle is one eighty minus sixty minus sixty
rendo line ki kooda same sixty degrees vasthundi
all three angles are sixty so it is equilateral

steps.why: Equal angles are enough here: a triangle with all three angles equal has all three sides equal, so no side length has to be computed to prove the shape.
common_mistakes: Showing only one angle is 60° and calling the triangle equilateral.
Taking the third angle as 60° by assumption instead of from the angle sum.

steps.label: Find the area
steps.margin_note: The last mark. The height from the origin to the given line is the perpendicular distance |n|/√(l² + m²). In an equilateral triangle the height is (√3/2) times the side, so the side follows from the height.
steps.memory_tip: Height of an equilateral triangle is (√3/2) × side, so side = 2 × height ÷ √3.
lines: L₁ and L₂ meet at O(0, 0), so the height
from O to L is d = |n| / √(l² + m²)
For an equilateral triangle of side s,

recall.must_convey: That the height is |n|/√(l² + m²), the side is 2d/√3, and the area (√3/4)s² gives n²/(√3(l² + m²)).
accept: the height is the perpendicular distance from the origin to the given line
in an equilateral triangle the height is root three by two times the side
area is root three by four times side squared
origin nunchi perpendicular distance ye height
the area comes out n squared over root three into l squared plus m squared

steps.why: Squaring the height removes the modulus, since |n|² = n². That is why the answer carries n² and not |n|. The result needs l² + m² ≠ 0 and n ≠ 0: with n = 0 the given line passes through the origin and there is no triangle, which is what the formula reports as area 0.
common_mistakes: Using d as the side length instead of the height.
Writing the area of an equilateral triangle as ½s² instead of (√3/4)s².
